subject: the FOOTGUNS.json -> CI shard link: the coverage decision, the active filter, and the shard list itself
_comment: M3 is the DELETION TEST the contract owes at every tier: remove one adopted suite from ci.yml and the live gate must go RED. M1/M2/M4 anchor ZERO-WIDTH on decisions in the gate, never on values. M3 note: bd-mutate refuses an empty 'new', so the suite is REPLACED by a name no shard should carry rather than deleted outright -- same effect on the decision under test, tests/test_route_map_invariant.py is no longer executed by any CI job. M5 is the bounce's second owed item: it pins HOW the exemption matches, not only what is in it. It widens the exact-key lookup into a stem prefix -- the shape a maintainer reaches for when a file is renamed -- and a widened match must turn something red.

mutants.label: M1 the exemption swallows every subject
M2 the active filter stops filtering
M3 DELETION TEST: one adopted suite is taken back out of the shard
M4 the spent-exemption check stops detecting a sharded exemption
M5 the exemption stops matching an exact path and matches by stem instead
mutants.new: return sorted(set(subjects) - set(executed) - {p for p in subjects if any(p.startswith(e[:-3]) for e in _EXEMPT)})
